University Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  4  
 
1. Introduction, Context and Principles 
 
1.1 This policy and SETU’s review framework will support the University to ensure 
quality and cognisance of best practice and developments in its provision of 
education and delivery of services, including any supporting infrastructure 
required. The review framework facilitates SETU’s compliance with both statutory 
and non-statutory obligations. Statutory bases for review include, but are not 
limited to: 
• 
Ensuring, in respect of each award made by the University that is recognised 
within the National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ), that each learner 
achieving an award has achieved the standard of knowledge, skill and 
competence associated with the award level (Qualifications and Quality 
Assurance [Education and Training] Act 2012 (as amended), s. 43 (6), (8)). 
• 
Establishing and undergoing reviews of the effectiveness of its quality 
assurance procedures and its procedures for access, transfer and progression 
(Qualifications and Quality Assurance [Education and Training] Act 2012 (as 
amended), s. 28, s. 34, s. 56, s. 57).  
 
1.2 The policy will also enable the University to meet emerging national and 
international requirements, legislative or otherwise, with regard to its provision of 
education and delivery of services.  
 
1.3 Furthermore, the policy will assist the University to meet the expectations of 
University stakeholders, and to assure them of the quality of its education provision 
and service delivery. Stakeholders include students and staff of SETU and its 
collaborative providers, employers and businesses, external bodies, other 
educational institutions, including those that engage in collaborative provision with 
SETU, and the State as a whole.  
 
1.4 This policy reflects the University’s commitment to continuous improvement, helps 
to ensure that periodic reviews of University education provision and service 
delivery take place, that the outcomes of these reviews are reported and acted upon 
appropriately, and that these outcomes are used to inform enhancements to the 
University’s provision of education and delivery of services. 
 
1.5 The University recognises the need for other bodies to support the effective 
implementation of this policy. In this regard, the University acknowledges the 
important contribution that professional statutory and regulatory bodies (PSRBs) 
make to quality assuring its provision. The University commits to engaging with 
these bodies to ensure complementarity between its review processes and the 
processes of PSRBs as well as to collaborating to reduce unnecessary administrative 
burden across processes, insofar as this is possible.

University Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  5  
 
1.6 In developing this policy, the University is guided and informed by the SETU Quality 
Framework document, the Standards and Guidelines for Quality Assurance in the 
European Higher Education Area (2015) and relevant policies and guidelines 
developed by Quality and Qualifications Ireland. 
 
 
2. Purpose 
 
2.1 The University Reviews Policy sets out the requirement for the University to 
conduct reviews of its education provision and service delivery. It also stipulates the 
types of reviews to be undertaken, the objectives, stages and outcomes of reviews, 
and the responsibilities of the University and relevant stakeholders involved in 
carrying out reviews. 
 
2.2 This policy creates the basis for the University to develop schedules of reviews and 
to request reviews on specific themes as necessary. 
 
2.3 Furthermore, this policy seeks to ensure that appropriate action is taken based on 
reviews conducted and that reviews support a cycle of continuous improvement in 
the University’s education provision and service delivery. 
 
 
3. Scope 
 
3.1 This policy applies to all SETU staff and students, as well as staff and students of 
third-party providers involved in the delivery of programmes leading to SETU 
awards as appropriate. Staff and students are required to engage with the policy as 
necessary and are expected to participate in and contribute to reviews as 
appropriate. 
 
4. Policy 
 
4.1 Types of Review 
Reviews can take place at any unit level; the appropriate level must be agreed with 
the relevant stakeholders, including the appropriate member(s) of the Executive 
Management Team, prior to commencement of planning for the review. In general, 
there is an expectation that normally a review will be at an organisational (i.e. cross-
campus) level. This policy addresses the following types of reviews:

University Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  6  
 
• Reviews of the University’s academic units, which will entail a review of the 
strategic direction of the unit in question, including its plans and objectives 
regarding subject development; a review of the unit’s teaching, learning and 
assessment strategies; a review of its research objectives, activities and outputs, 
benchmarking these against international best practice; and a review of taught 
and research programmes, including programmes provided collaboratively. Such 
reviews will usually be at faculty or departmental level, but may, alternatively, 
focus on smaller units within a Faculty or Department; 
• Reviews of University services, which can address any service delivered by the 
University, or any professional service area or activity within the University; 
• Thematic reviews, which are reviews of specific themes identified by relevant 
University bodies (including, but not limited to, the Joint Quality Committee, 
Academic Council and Governing Body), and which represent areas of particular 
interest to the University. 
 
4.2 Review Objectives 
The objectives of University reviews are, as relevant and appropriate to the 
unit/area/activity reviewed, to: 
• Ensure that the component units of the University are supporting the 
University’s strategic direction; 
• Quality assure the unit/area/activity in question and benchmark it against other 
similar instances of education provision/service delivery; 
• Identify key challenges and opportunities; 
• Identify and respond to new developments; 
• Identify areas of good practice that can be disseminated across the University; 
• Identify potential quality enhancements and plan for their implementation; 
• Recognise and respond to perceived weaknesses; 
• Elicit feedback from SETU’s constituents and stakeholders to contribute to the 
continuous improvement of the University’s provision; 
• Review the effectiveness of quality assurance procedures. 
 
4.3 Review Schedules 
The way in which reviews are initiated and scheduled will depend on the type of 
review. Statutory reviews will be initiated and scheduled in accordance with the 
University’s statutory obligations. Academic unit, and professional service area and 
activity reviews will occur as part of an agreed schedule, which will be agreed by 
the Joint Quality Committee. Thematic reviews will arise from time to time (in 
general, the University will aim to undertake one thematic review per academic 
year).

University Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  7  
 
4.4 Key Review Stages 
The key stages in a University review, in summary, are (for the relevant 
unit/area/activity): 
a. Agreement of a timeline and terms of reference for the review process 
between management of the unit/area/activity and the Office of the Vice 
President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning. Each review process 
will occur as part of the overall review schedule established by the Joint 
Quality Committee. 
b. Engagement by unit/area/activity members and relevant internal and 
external stakeholders of the unit/area/activity in a self-evaluation process.  
c. Preparation of a self-evaluation report by unit/area/activity members 
through a self-evaluation committee. 
d. Establishment of an independent peer review group and approval of peer 
review group composition by the Joint Quality Committee.  
e. Review of the self-evaluation report (as part of a broader engagement 
process, typically including a site visit and meetings with relevant internal 
and external stakeholders) by a peer review group. 
f. Preparation of a peer review group report, to include recommendations of 
the peer review group. 
g. Consideration of the peer review group report by the unit/area/activity 
members, including the relevant executive lead. 
h. Development of a quality enhancement plan and executive response arising 
from the report.  
i. Consideration of the outcome of the review process, including any 
recommendations, and approval of the quality enhancement plan, by the 
University (Academic Council and Governing Body will consider the 
outcomes of and responses to academic unit and thematic reviews; 
Governing Body will consider the outcomes of professional service area 
reviews). 
j. Publication of the peer review group report on the University website to 
ensure transparency and dissemination of good practice and to promote 
public confidence. 
k. Ongoing monitoring by the University of the quality enhancement plan’s 
implementation by means of submission of an annual update on 
implementation to the Joint Quality Committee. 
 
4.5 Review Guidelines 
Members of units/areas/activities undergoing review will be supported by 
guidelines for review processes, which will be maintained by the Office of the Vice 
President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning.

University Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
  | P a g e  8  
 
4.6 Self-evaluation Process and Report 
Responsibility to produce self-evaluation reports rests with management of the 
unit/area/activity. To support consistency of approach across the University, the 
Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning will 
develop and maintain a template for self-evaluation reports. 
4.7 Peer Review Group Composition 
The peer review group should include an appropriate balance of expertise and 
experience and should comprise a suitably qualified chair, an appropriate number 
of external academic and/or professional representatives relevant to the 
unit/area/activity, an external student representative, and a secretary, who is 
responsible for drafting the peer review group report, from the Office of the Vice 
President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning. The University will have 
regard to international representation and gender balance in establishing the peer 
review group. 
 
5. Responsibilities 
 
5.1 Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning 
 
5.1.1 
The organisation and operational management of University reviews is the 
responsibility of the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, 
Teaching and Learning, in consultation with the management of the 
unit/area/activity. 
 
5.1.2 
Peer review group members will be provided with appropriate briefing and 
training by the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching 
and Learning to ensure their familiarity with the University’s context and 
that of the unit/area/activity under review. 
 
5.2 Joint Quality Committee 
The Joint Quality Committee is responsible for the formation of the reviews policy, 
for approving the schedule of University reviews, for approving the composition of 
and appointing peer review groups, for ensuring that reviews are taking place and 
being reported on, and for ensuring that reviews are being completed and their 
outcomes implemented. 
 
5.3 Executive Management Team 
For academic unit or professional service unit reviews, the relevant Executive is 
responsible for considering the outcome of the review, drafting an executive

response to the recommendations (which will focus on the financial impact of the 
quality enhancement plan) and submitting the quality enhancement plan for 
approval to Governing Body (for professional service unit reviews) or to Academic 
Council and Governing Body (for academic unit reviews).  
 
5.4 Academic Council 
Academic Council is responsible for the approval of the outcomes of reviews of 
academic units – to include any recommendations, as well as the quality 
enhancement plan – and monitoring the plan’s implementation by the academic 
unit. 
 
5.5 Unit under Review 
The unit under review is responsible for undertaking a comprehensive self-
evaluation exercise of its activities, ensuring that all relevant stakeholders, internal 
and external to the unit, are involved in and/or consulted on the process. It must 
then record the process and its outcomes in a self-evaluation report. The unit under 
review is also responsible for ensuring that a representative selection of relevant 
internal and external stakeholders is available to meet with the peer review group 
during the site visit. Following the production of the review report, the unit under 
review will develop a quality enhancement plan, setting out how it intends 
responding to and implementing any conditions and/or recommendations issued 
by the peer review group. As outlined above, the unit’s implementation of the 
quality enhancement plan will be monitored by the University. 
 
5.6 Final Approval of Review Outcomes 
The final approval of the outcomes of all University reviews, as well as monitoring 
of the related quality enhancement plans, is provided by Governing Body and/or 
Academic Council as appropriate depending on the nature of the review.

7. Review of Policy 
 
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date, and/or as soon as 
possible following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
8. Author 
 
The author of this policy is the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, 
Teaching and Learning. Any feedback or issues arising on implementation of this 
policy should be communicated to the policy author. The policy author is 
responsible for ensuring that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when 
reviewing the policy. 
9. Compliance 
 
It is expected that all employees will comply with this policy.
